```{python}
#| include: false
from IPython.display import HTML, display

import acme_metrics as m

ev = m.load()
```

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(m.banner(ev))
```

```{python}
display(HTML(m.tiles([
    ("Round", str(ev.round or "—"), f"rounds in file: {', '.join(map(str, ev.rounds)) or 'none'}"),
    ("Cases run", f"{len(ev.run)}/{len(ev.frame)}", "with a workflow decision"),
    ("Reviewed", f"{len(ev.reviewed)}/{len(ev.frame)}", "Pass or Fail from the expert"),
    ("Drafting model", ev.provenance()["drafting model"], "from the saved runs"),
])))
```

| Page | Answers | For |

| [Dataset card](dataset-card.qmd) | Is the test fair? What it covers, where cases come from, open label decisions, and what it can't tell you. | Anyone trusting the numbers |

: {tbl-colwidths="[22,53,25]"}

**Refreshing.** These pages only read files. After reviewing in the Studio, re-render from `acme-review-studio/`:

```bash
quarto render reports                                  # whole site → reports/_site/
quarto render reports/evaluation-report.qmd -P review_round:2
```

The definitions live in one place, `reports/acme_metrics.py`, and the release gates and error costs in `reports/thresholds.yml`.
